title: MEDDIC, MEDDICC and MEDDPICC explained
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no author or date shown). MEDDIC was created at PTC in 1996 by Dick Dunkel, with Jack Napoli also credited; MEDDIC is Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Identify Pain, Champion; MEDDICC adds Competition; MEDDPICC adds Paper Process and uses Implicate the Pain; presented as a way to qualify deals early and a common language for deal health. Site of a MEDDICC training business.

title: MEDDICC: The definitive guide to MEDDPICC (book page)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Book by Andy Whyte; the page names Dick Dunkel as co-creator of the original MEDDIC methodology. Publication year not stated on the page.

title: Set up and manage object pipelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 29 September 2026. Each deal stage has a win probability used for weighted amounts; conditional stage properties can be made required before a record is created in or moved to a stage; pipeline rules can control editing and require approval; custom pipeline limits by subscription (Starter 15, Professional 100 or 350, Enterprise 350, free tools none).

title: Associate records
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 16 September 2026. Association labels describe how records relate (examples given: manager, advisor) and need a Professional or Enterprise subscription; the default Primary label marks a contact's primary company.

title: Create and send quotes
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 28 October 2026. Creating quotes needs Revenue Hub Professional or Enterprise and a Revenue Hub seat; quotes that need approval move to Pending approval until approvers act; e-signature is the default acceptance method; a default expiration period can be set.

title: Understand HubSpot CPQ
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 12 October 2026. CPQ is available with Revenue Hub Professional and Enterprise; standard and advanced quote approvals; advanced approvals (Enterprise) route on discounts, amounts and term lengths; quote rules can warn or block publishing.

title: HubSpot MCP server
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Remote MCP server with read and write access to contacts, companies, deals, quotes, line items and engagements (calls, emails, meetings, notes, tasks); users, owners and teams read-only; access set by a user-level app's scopes; an account admin connects first.

title: Sales Cloud pricing
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Lists a Free Suite and paid editions (Starter Suite, Pro Suite, Core, Advanced, Max), most with free trials, and Agentforce for Sales as an add-on; the page says it is subject to change. Salesforce Help pages (for example Account Plans) did not load for automated checks on 6 November 2026.

title: Salesforce DX MCP server end of life (forcedotcom/mcp issue 46)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Salesforce DX local MCP server reached end of life on 2 November 2026 and its repositories are archived; Salesforce says its tooling is now delivered as skills.

title: Dealings with competitors
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no page date shown). Many collaborations between competitors are lawful, including joint ventures; risk arises when they stop acting independently; price fixing, bid rigging and market or customer division are treated as always illegal.

title: Horizontal agreements: guidance
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 16 August 2023; explains how the Chapter I prohibition of the Competition Act 1998 applies to agreements between actual or potential competitors, alongside the specialisation and R&D block exemptions.

title: Horizontal block exemption regulations and guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Revised R&D and specialisation block exemption regulations adopted 1 June 2023; revised Horizontal Guidelines published in the Official Journal on 21 July 2023.

title: FAR Subpart 9.6: Contractor Team Arrangements
supports: Opened with WebFetch; FAC 2026-01, effective 13 March 2026. A team arrangement is a partnership or joint venture acting as prime, or a prime with agreed subcontractors; the government recognises arrangements when members and relationships are disclosed in the offer; the subpart does not authorise arrangements that break antitrust law.

title: SBA Mentor-Protege Program
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A mentor and protege may form a joint venture to bid as a small business if the protege qualifies as small; the protege performs at least 40% of the joint venture's work; agreements last up to six years; processing takes about 105 days; the 8(a) and All Small programmes merged on 16 November 2020.

title: How to win contracts
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Marketing to government: learn what agencies or primes need and show how you meet it; agency small business offices (OSDBU or OSBP) and Procurement Center Representatives; SUBNet lists subcontracting opportunities from large primes.

title: Basic requirements for federal contracting
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Register in SAM to contract with the government; a UEI is a 12-character alphanumeric ID assigned at SAM registration; match services to NAICS codes (more than one allowed); SBA size standards per NAICS code.

title: Directive 2014/24/EU on public procurement
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Article 19(2): groups of economic operators, including temporary associations, may take part and cannot be required to have a specific legal form to submit a tender; Article 19(3): a legal form may be required after award where needed for performance.

title: Small and medium business hub
supports: Opened with WebFetch; updated 21 July 2026, when Crown Commercial Service references became Government Commercial Agency. Public notices are on Find a Tender, where suppliers register before bidding; government aims to pay 90% of invoices within 5 days and all within 30; since 1 September 2019, bidders for central government contracts over 5 million GBP a year must show they pay 95% of supply chain invoices within 60 days.

title: Employers' liability insurance
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Employers need cover of at least 5 million GBP from an authorised insurer as soon as they employ someone (exemptions include employing only a close family member); fine of 2,500 GBP a day without proper cover and 1,000 GBP for not displaying the certificate, which may be shown electronically.

title: Cyber Essentials overview
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Government-recommended minimum standard based on five technical controls; Cyber Essentials Plus adds independent technical testing; IASME is the delivery partner and runs certification.

title: Bribery Act 2010 guidance
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 11 February 2012, updated 22 January 2025; section 7 offence of failing to prevent bribery by associated persons; adequate procedures are a defence; six principles: proportionality, top-level commitment, risk assessment, due diligence, communication and monitoring and review.

title: Find and update company information
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Search the register by company name, number or officer; view company data and document images; search for disqualified directors.

title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
supports: Opened with WebFetch. No exception for business-to-business email; accurate headers, honest subject lines, ad disclosure, a postal address and an opt-out; opt-outs honoured within 10 business days; up to 53,088 USD per violating email; the sender stays responsible for email sent on its behalf.

title: Marketing and advertising: the law (direct marketing)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Marketing messages must identify the sender and make clear they are selling; every marketing email needs an unsubscribe option; check the Telephone Preference Service before telesales calls; opting out must be easy.

title: Directive 2002/58/EC (ePrivacy Directive), consolidated 19 December 2009
publisher: EUR-Lex, Publications Office of the European Union
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Article 13(1): prior consent for email marketing; 13(2): soft opt-in for a company's own similar products to existing customers; 13(5): protection of business (non-individual) subscribers is left to EU and national law.

title: Talk-to-listen ratio analysis
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 21 August 2025, modified 4 March 2026: 326,000 sales calls of 10 minutes or more; sellers talked 60% on average, 57% in won deals and 62% in lost deals. Vendor data.
